The image shows a mango leaf with significant edge damage — irregular, ragged tissue loss along the leaf margin, with brown/necrotic edges and torn-looking tissue. The leaf surface itself appears mostly green but the margins are heavily chewed/cut away in an irregular pattern.

Key observations:
- Ragged, irregular cuts along leaf margin
- Brown necrotic tissue at cut edges
- Tissue removal pattern suggests physical feeding/cutting damage
- Not a fungal coating (no white powder, no black sooty layer)
- Not a canker or die-back pattern (which affect stems/branches)
- The irregular margin cutting is characteristic of weevil feeding damage

This pattern strongly matches **Cutting_Weevil** — these insects cut characteristic irregular notches from leaf margins, leaving ragged brown edges exactly as seen here.
